option_assessments.assessment: Best single-feature reading: controlled experiment and observation indicate management as a science.
Incorrect; no professional qualification, association, or code-of-conduct feature is described.
Possible if focus is the manager's practical application of skill, but the stem foregrounds experiment.
Reasonably defensible: practical implementation can be art while the experiment is scientific; stem does not isolate one nature.

decisive_assumptions_or_source_gaps: The stem does not isolate whether the highlighted feature is experimental method (science) or practical application (art); A and D can both fit its described actions.
records.independent_explanation: Experimentation and observation are science cues, so A is the likely intended answer. Because the manager also applies a practical intervention and the stem asks broadly which nature is highlighted, D has a reasonable reading; abstain under the unique-answer gate.
cuet_fit_reasons: Four-option objective format and in-syllabus topic fit CUET, but the defensible second answer blocks readiness under the single-answer correctness gate.

option_assessments.assessment: Correct under the modal can: control action can prevent recurrence of deviations; the reason gives the mechanism.
Incorrect: R directly explains how controlling can prevent recurrence, even though it says minimise rather than guarantee zero deviations.
Incorrect: R is true; it describes reducing recurrence through action.
Incorrect under the ordinary modal reading: controlling can prevent recurrence, though it does not ensure that every deviation will be prevented.

decisive_assumptions_or_source_gaps: The assertion uses can, not always or will; its truth depends on the ordinary ability/possibility reading. The supplied excerpt supports preventing recurrence after deviations, not preventing every deviation from first occurring.
records.independent_explanation: R is true and explains A when can means that corrective control action has the capacity to prevent recurrence. It would be false only under an absolute reading that controlling invariably prevents every deviation, which the stem does not say.
cuet_fit_reasons: Short assertion-reason item on a core control function; modality is a small but reasonable reading demand.

records.subject: economics

option_assessments.assessment: Correct on the NCERT institutional reading: government may act through the central bank entrusted to conduct these purchases on its behalf, and the resulting reserve/money-supply increase addresses a deflationary gap.
Incorrect on that reading because the increase in reserves/money supply is precisely the mechanism that explains the claimed counter-deflationary effect.
Incorrect on the delegated-agent reading: the reason is supported by the NCERT description of central-bank purchases and reserves.
Incorrect on the delegated-agent reading: both propositions are true, with R explaining the mechanism.

decisive_assumptions_or_source_gaps: Government must mean government acting through the central bank; NCERT says OMO purchases are entrusted to the central bank on behalf of government. If the assertion means the government itself independently executes an OMO, the actor is inaccurate and D becomes plausible.
records.independent_explanation: The NCERT excerpt states that the central bank buys government bonds on behalf of government and the purchase raises reserves and money supply. With government understood as acting through that agent, both A and R are true and R supplies the expansionary mechanism. The actor shorthand lowers confidence.
cuet_fit_reasons: Money-and-banking topic and assertion-reason format fit the syllabus, but the government/central-bank actor ambiguity can change a proposition's truth and prevents a confident single key.

option_assessments.assessment: Incorrect: gross product taxes omit product subsidies, which must be netted.
Correct: add net product taxes (product taxes less product subsidies) to GVA at basic prices.
Incorrect: production taxes are not product taxes and are not the stated conversion item.
Incorrect: net production taxes retain the product-versus-production category error.

decisive_assumptions_or_source_gaps: The supplied IES excerpt says net product tax and product subsidies; interpret this as taxes on products less subsidies on products. It does not support replacing product taxes with production taxes.
records.independent_explanation: GVA at market prices equals GVA at basic prices plus product taxes minus product subsidies. Therefore the required addition is net product taxes.
cuet_fit_reasons: Central national-income aggregate conversion, direct conceptual recall, and concise four-option presentation fit CUET pacing.

option_assessments.assessment: Incorrect: revenue deficit requires revenue expenditure and revenue receipts, which are not given.
Correct: fiscal deficit = total expenditure - total receipts excluding borrowings = 45 - 27.2 = 17.8 lakh crore.
Incorrect: budgetary deficit is not the specified modern definition; the stated receipts measure identifies fiscal deficit.
Incorrect: primary deficit requires subtracting interest payments from fiscal deficit, and interest payments are not supplied.

decisive_assumptions_or_source_gaps: None decisive; the supplied NCERT definition matches the given operands.
records.independent_explanation: 45.0 - 27.2 = 17.8 lakh crore. Total receipts other than borrowings are non-borrowing receipts, so the difference is fiscal deficit.
cuet_fit_reasons: One-step arithmetic using the core fiscal-deficit definition; relevant data are complete and estimated time is well below the threshold.

option_assessments.assessment: Correct: MPC can equal one; Statement 2 is false because consumption's increase cannot exceed the income increase, so it is not always proportionately greater.
Incorrect: Statement 1 is true and Statement 2 is false.
Incorrect: Statement 2's always claim is false.
Incorrect: Statement 1 is true.

decisive_assumptions_or_source_gaps: Interpret proportionately greater as delta consumption / delta income greater than one. The supplied NCERT excerpt directly states the maximum MPC is one and change in consumption cannot exceed change in income.
records.independent_explanation: The excerpt sets the maximum MPC at 1, so Statement 1 is true. An increase in consumption is not always proportionately greater than the increase in income; that would require MPC greater than one, so Statement 2 is false.

records.subject: economics

option_assessments.assessment: Incorrect: induced investment is not in the stated simple two-sector model; investment is autonomous.
Incorrect: induced investment is not included.
Incorrect: omits induced consumption, which is part of household consumption when income varies.
Correct: AD = C + I; C includes autonomous and induced consumption, and I is autonomous.

decisive_assumptions_or_source_gaps: The stem explicitly sets the NCERT two-sector model with autonomous investment; no induced-investment term is assumed.
records.independent_explanation: In the two-sector model, aggregate demand is consumption plus investment. Consumption contains autonomous and income-induced parts, while the question stipulates that investment is autonomous. Thus the three components are autonomous consumption, induced consumption, and autonomous investment.
cuet_fit_reasons: Core two-sector aggregate-demand decomposition, short reading, and one-step conceptual application fit standard CUET objective format.
